subject: Security notification: obligations, evidence handover, and cross-border data transfer
messages:
From: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@finex.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Katie Ramirez <katie.ramirez@finex.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify notification & evidence-transfer expectations

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. As we prepare the DPA and incident annex, the legal team asked for clarity on a few items so we can align with our internal incident response and regulatory reporting timelines:

- Initial notification window: do you commit to an "initial" notification timeframe (e.g., 24/48/72 hours) for confirmed incidents affecting regulated data?
- Evidence handover: what is Redwood willing to provide (logs, full forensic image, KV cache snapshots) and within what window?
- Cross-border transfers: if evidence must be exported to our EU team, are there restrictions or additional approvals needed for Redwood subprocessors?
- Forensics vendor: will Redwood permit the use of a customer-appointed forensics firm to collect or receive artifacts directly?

We want to avoid a long contract negotiation over each incident; if you can share proposed contractual language for these points (scope, timelines, vendor access, and any limitations) that would be helpful.

Best,
Alex
Alex Dawson
CISO, Finex Financial Services

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@finex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify notification & evidence-transfer expectations

Alex — thanks, good questions. High-level position below; Marissa (legal) and Vivek (security ops) are looped for specifics and any absolute limits. I'll also attach our incident timeline template.

Summary position (draft):
- Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial confirmation of a material security incident involving regulated customer data within 48 hours of identification (or sooner if we can confirm earlier).
- Evidence scope & window: Redwood will make available requestable artifacts: request logs, delivery metadata, and relevant KV-cache/sequence metadata. Full forensic images are sensitive and subject to a scoped request; for those we propose a targeted evidence-handover window of up to 7 calendar days following a mutually agreed scope and approval.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood will not export customer data to a third country without customer consent; we propose an explicit clause requiring customer approval for transfers to a customer's EU/cross-border forensics team.
- Forensics vendor: Customer-appointed vendors may be allowed on a read-only receipt basis or via joint collection if approved by Redwood. We require an executed NDA and scoped statement of work for vendor access.

I'll let Marissa and Vivek add precise contract text and any required SLAs. Attaching: timeline_template.xlsx, subprocessor_list_v2.pdf.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Security Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@finex.com>, Katie Ramirez <katie.ramirez@finex.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Suggested contract text and limits (draft)

Team / Alex — drafting proposed contract language below. This is intentionally narrow to avoid broad obligations we can't operationalize. Feedback welcome.

Proposed language (draft):
1) Initial notification. "Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to notify Customer of a confirmed security incident affecting Customer data within forty-eight (48) hours of Provider's identification of the incident. Such notification shall include a summary of impact, affected datasets (by customer ID), and immediate mitigating actions taken."

2) Evidence scope and delivery. "Following initial notification, upon Customer's written request Provider shall, within seven (7) calendar days, provide mutually agreed data artifacts necessary for Customer's investigation, which may include request/operation logs, delivery metadata, and logical snapshots of relevant in-memory cache state. Production of full disk images or raw hardware exports is not a standard deliverable; such requests will be considered on a case-by-case basis and may require additional approvals, cost recovery, and an executed addendum."

3) Customer-appointed forensics. "Customer may propose a third-party forensics vendor. Provider will permit, subject to Provider's prior written approval, the transfer of agreed artifacts to the vendor or a joint collection conducted under Provider supervision. Provider reserves the right to require an NDA, limited-scope SOW, and to be present or participate for chain-of-custody purposes."

4) Cross-border transfers. "Provider will not export Customer data outside the EEA where Customer has prohibited such transfer. Customer may grant specific written consent for transfers to Customer-appointed entities in other jurisdictions."

5) Subprocessors. "Provider will notify Customer of material changes to the subprocessor list at least thirty (30) days prior to onboarding and will honor reasonable data handling restrictions necessary to comply with Customer's regulatory obligations."

Operational notes: Vivek — can you confirm whether the 7-day delivery window is operationally feasible for the artifacts listed? Aditya — I'll need a short paragraph for sales (customer-facing summary) that positions this as "cooperative, scoped, and auditable" rather than a full image handover promise.

—Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suggested contract text and limits (draft)

Marissa — operationally OK with caveats. Quick notes inline: 
- 48-hour initial notification: feasible as a contractual SLA for confirmed incidents. We will need an internal classification step (identification -> confirmation) and a war-room process; if triage cannot confirm in 48 hours we can provide "initial advisory" within 24 hours and a confirmed incident notification by 48 hours.
- 7-day artifact window: acceptable for logical artifacts and logs. Full forensic images: require hardware-level approvals and will likely take longer (we should call this out as "subject to reasonable delay for collection and export controls").
- Chain-of-custody: must be preserved; if customer vendor collects directly, Redwood must validate vendor credentials and execute an evidentiary collection SOW.

Alex — for your team: propose we exchange a short evidence-handover checklist (I've attached a draft "forensic_evidence_request.docx") that lists the categories of artifacts, expected format, and contact points. This will speed decisions during an incident.

—Vivek
VP, Security Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@finex.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Katie Ramirez <katie.ramirez@finex.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suggested contract text and limits (draft)

Thanks — this is helpful and a lot closer to what we need. A couple of redlines from Legal / IR perspective: 

- Can we codify an "initial advisory" within 24 hours and a confirmed notice within 48? That meets our internal regulator expectations.
- We need a maximum calendar window for handing over requested artifacts (logs, metadata) of 7 calendar days from the time of written request; agree that full disk images may take longer but request that Redwood provide an interim plan within 48 hours of request for any artifact expected to exceed 7 days.
- For cross-border transfers: Finex will provide destination and purpose. We require that Redwood not unreasonably withhold approval for transfers to our EU forensics team; proposed wording: "Provider shall not unreasonably deny a Customer request to transfer investigative artifacts to Customer-appointed EU-based forensic providers; any denial must be accompanied by written reasoning within 48 hours."
- Forensics vendor: we will ensure an NDA and SOW; Finex asks that the vendor be permitted to receive copies of agreed artifacts directly once approvals are in place.

If you can incorporate these points into a redlined DPA annex, we can move this to doc-signing quickly. Also: Vivek's checklist looks good — please include it in the annex as an exhibit.

Appreciate the speed.

Best,
Alex
CISO, Finex Financial Services
